result.topic_en: Calculus of variations: the first variation of an integral depending on y and its derivatives, the resulting Euler–Lagrange expression, its extension to several functions, and side conditions handled with Lagrange multipliers.
result.transcription:
$W = \int_a^b F(x, y, y', y'', y''') \, dx$
$y + \delta y \quad \delta y = h\eta$.
[-$y'+$-] $\delta y' = \frac{\partial(\delta y)}{\partial x} \quad \delta y'' = \frac{\partial^2(\delta y)}{\partial x^2}$
$\delta W = \int_a^b \left( \frac{\partial F}{\partial y}\delta y + \frac{\partial F}{\partial y'}\delta y' + \frac{\partial F}{\partial y''}\delta y'' + \quad \right) dx$
$\int \frac{\partial F}{\partial y'} \frac{\partial \delta y}{\partial x} dx = \frac{\partial F}{\partial y'}\delta y - \int \delta y \frac{\partial \left(\frac{\partial F}{\partial y'}\right)}{\partial x} dx$.
$\delta W = \int_a^b P \delta y \, dx + \cdots$
$P = \frac{\partial F}{\partial y} - \frac{\partial\left(\frac{\partial F}{\partial y'}\right)}{\partial x} + \frac{\partial^2\left(\frac{\partial F}{\partial y''}\right)}{\partial x^2} - \frac{\partial^3\left(\frac{\partial F}{\partial y'''}\right)}{\partial x^3}$
$W = \int_a^b F(x, y_1, y_1', y_1'' \cdots, y_2, y_2', y_2'' [?], y_3, y_3' \cdots)$
$y_1 + \delta y_1 \quad y_2 + \delta y_2 \quad y_3 + \delta y_3$.
$\delta W = \int_a^b (P\delta y_1 + Q\delta y_2 + R\delta y_3) dx$
$P = 0 \quad Q = 0 \quad R = 0$
[-$\mathfrak{L}$[?]-] $u = 0 \quad v = 0$
$\delta u = 0 \quad \delta v = 0$
$= \frac{\partial u}{\partial y_1}\delta y_1 + \frac{\partial u}{\partial y_2}\delta y_2$
$P\delta y_1 + Q\delta y_2 + R\delta y_3 + \lambda \delta u + \mu \delta v \cdots$
[-$\int_a$-] $\delta W + \delta\int_a^b \lambda u \, dx + \delta \int_a^b \mu v \, dx + \cdots = 0$
